content.text:
What's amazing about the brain and heart?

The brain that lets us think and feel, and the heart that beats without ever resting, are the two most important organs in our body. They're hard at work right now, too.

content.alt: The Story of the Brain and Heart - Nature and science facts about the brain and heart
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the brain and heart

The brain weighs about 1.4 kg and has around 86 billion nerve cells that exchange information through electrical signals. It's so busy that it uses about 25% of the body's oxygen, and it organizes memories while we sleep. The heart beats 60–100 times a minute, over 100,000 times a day, sending blood throughout the body. If you laid out all the blood vessels in our body, they'd stretch more than twice around the Earth.

content.alt: The Story of the Brain and Heart - Points worth exploring together
content.text:
Points worth exploring together

Point out things like the brain (thinking, memory, sleep), the heart (beating, sending blood), the heart rate (100,000 times a day), and blood vessels (very long). It's fun to talk together about "Why does the heart beat without ever resting?"

content.alt: The Story of the Brain and Heart - Parent guide — how to spark curiosity
content.text:
Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Place a hand on the chest to feel the heartbeat, then observe how it speeds up after jumping in place. Teaching "When you sleep well, your brain organizes memories" also helps build good sleep habits.
content.caption: Observing the heartbeat

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How many times a day does the heart beat?
A. Over 100,000 times a day. Without ever resting, it sends oxygen-rich blood throughout the body.

Q. What does the brain do while we sleep?
A. It organizes and strengthens memories and clears out waste. That's why sleep is so important.

Q. How can we explore this at home?
A. Feel the heartbeat with a hand on the chest, observe the faster beat after running, and talk about good sleep habits.
